copy.heading: Choose how your agents think
copy.body: Keep your accounts directly with the model companies and use your own subscriptions or API keys.
Ronin does not resell model access and does not place itself between you and the provider. The credential is written by the provider's own CLI and stays on this machine.
One working provider is enough to move on. Add the rest whenever you like.

copy.heading: Introduce yourself
copy.body: Registering gives you access to Ronin Services and lets you take part in the Bounty Program. Both are free.
It is not required. Ronin works without it, and Services already installed stay usable either way.

media.label: Registration and Services
media.description: What registering establishes, and what it does not gate

copy.heading: Choose a Workspace Folder
copy.body: Workspace Folders are your project roots: real directories on this machine and GitHub repositories. They give your agents known surfaces to work on.
Add the directory or repository holding the project you want worked on. You can register more at any time.
Authenticate with GitHub to work on remote repositories as well as folders already on this machine.

For a repository, choose how Agents work in it: a desk gives each Agent its own branch and working tree, which suits active code editing. A shared checkout keeps everyone in one tree, which suits notes, research and planning.

media.label: Workspace Folders
media.description: What a Workspace Folder is, and how to choose one

copy.heading: Choose installations
copy.body: Installations add optional facilities. The core coworkspace stays local and light without any of them.
Skip anything you are unsure about. An installation can be added the day you need it.
Installations maintained by the Ronin team ask that you register first. They are open code and not charged for.
In return, Ronin collects aggregate tool-use counts — never your code, prompts or messages — and asks that you do not commercialize the tools.

copy.heading: Start one Agent
copy.body: Everything before this was setup. This is the part that does work.
Give the Agent one clear objective, small enough that you can check the result yourself.
Set its reach: discuss talks it through, plan plans, execute completes the agreed work.
